58702-the-cricket-of-abel-hirst-and-shre.title: Thirty-Four Photographs
58702-the-cricket-of-abel-hirst-and-shre.creator: Mason And Basebe_
58702-the-cricket-of-abel-hirst-and-shre.description: A book by Mason And Basebe_. set him on the track of independent research and self-instruction: to show him how to watch and _see_, and how to practise the best things that he sees, and what the best things are most likely to be.

arxiv-1603-01770.title: An Argument-based Creative Assistant for Harmonic Blending Paper type: System Description Paper
arxiv-1603-01770.creator: Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas, Roberto Confalonieri, Joseph Corneli, Asterios Zacharakis and Emilios Cambouropoulos
arxiv-1603-01770.description: Abstract Conceptual blending is a powerful tool for computational creativity where, for example, the properties of two harmonic spaces may be combined in a consistent manner to produce a novel harmonic space. However, deciding about the importance of property features in the input spaces and evaluating the results of conceptual blending is a nontrivial task.

arxiv-2105-10655.title: ON CERTAIN REGULAR NICELY DISTANCE–BALANCED GRAPHS
arxiv-2105-10655.creator: Blas Fernández, Štefko Miklavič, Safet Penjić
arxiv-2105-10655.description: Abstract A connected graph Γ \Gamma is called nicely distance–balanced , whenever there exists a positive integer γ = γ ⁡ ( Γ ) \gamma=\gamma(\Gamma) , such that for any two adjacent vertices u , v u,v of Γ \Gamma there are exactly γ \gamma vertices of Γ \Gamma which are closer to u u than to v v ,

arxiv-2201-02008.title: Sparsity-based Feature Selection for Anomalous Subgroup Discovery
arxiv-2201-02008.creator: Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, William Ogallo, Catherine Wanjiru, Charles Wachira, Isaiah Onando Mulang’, Vibha Anand, Aisha Walcott-Bryant, Skyler Speakman
arxiv-2201-02008.description: Abstract Anomalous pattern detection aims to identify instances where deviation from normalcy is evident, and is widely applicable across domains. Multiple anomalous detection techniques have been proposed in the state of the art. However, there is a common lack of a principled and scalable feature selection method for efficient discovery.

arxiv-2208-13814.title: Non-trivial class of anisotropic compact stellar model in Rastall gravity Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2208-13814.creator: G.G.L. Nashed e1,addr1, W. El Hanafy e2,addr1
arxiv-2208-13814.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by G.G.L. Nashed e1,addr1, W. El Hanafy e2,addr1. We investigated Rastall gravity, for an anisotropic star with a static spherical symmetry, whereas the matter-geometry coupling as assumed in Rastall Theory (RT) is expected to play a crucial role differentiating RT from General Relativity (GR). Indeed, all the obtained results confirm that RT is not equivalent to GR, however, it produces same amount of anisotropy as GR for static spherically symmetric stellar models.

arxiv-2304-07238.title: Robustness of community structure under edge addition
arxiv-2304-07238.creator: Moyi Tian, Pablo Moriano
arxiv-2304-07238.description: Abstract Communities often represent key structural and functional clusters in networks. To preserve such communities, it is important to understand their robustness under network perturbations. Previous work in community robustness analysis has focused on studying changes in the community structure as a response of edge rewiring and node or edge removal.

arxiv-2308-02945.title: RV-CURE: A RISC-V Capability Architecture for Full Memory Safety
arxiv-2308-02945.creator: Yonghae Kim Georgia Institute of Technology yonghae@gatech.edu, Anurag Kar Georgia Institute of Technology anurag.kar@gatech.edu, Jaewon Lee Georgia Institute of Technology jaewon.lee@gatech.edu, Jaekyu Lee Arm Research jaekyu.lee@arm.com, Hyesoon Kim Georgia Institute of Technology hyesoon@cc.gatec
arxiv-2308-02945.description: Abstract Despite decades of efforts to resolve, memory safety violations are still persistent and problematic in modern systems. Various defense mechanisms have been proposed, but their deployment in real systems remains challenging because of performance, security, or compatibility concerns. In this paper, we propose RV-CURE , a RISC-V capability architecture that implements full-system support for full memory safety.

arxiv-2310-18435.title: Expanding the Set of Pragmatic Considerations in Conversational AI
arxiv-2310-18435.creator: S.M. Seals, Valerie L. Shalin
arxiv-2310-18435.description: Abstract Despite considerable performance improvements, current conversational AI systems often fail to meet user expectations. We discuss several pragmatic limitations of current conversational AI systems. We illustrate pragmatic limitations with examples that are syntactically appropriate, but have clear pragmatic deficiencies.

arxiv-2311-11213.title: Diverse features of dust particles and their aggregates inferred from experimental nanoparticles
arxiv-2311-11213.creator: Yuki Nakano, Yuki Kimura, Akihiko Hashimoto
arxiv-2311-11213.description: Abstract Nanometre- to micrometre-sized solid dust particles play a vital role in star and planet formations. Despite of their importance, however, our understanding of physical and chemical properties of dust particles is still provisional. We have conducted a condensation experiment of the vapour generated from a solid starting material having nearly cosmic proportions in elements.

arxiv-2402-09941.title: FedLion: Faster Adaptive Federated Optimization with Fewer Communication
arxiv-2402-09941.creator: Zhiwei Tang, Tsung-Hui Chang
arxiv-2402-09941.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhiwei Tang, Tsung-Hui Chang. In Federated Learning (FL), a framework to train machine learning models across distributed data, well-known algorithms like FedAvg tend to have slow convergence rates, resulting in high communication costs during training. To address this challenge, we introduce FedLion, an adaptive federated optimization algorithm that seamlessly incorporates key elements from the recently proposed centralized adaptive algorithm, Lion [ 1 ] , into the FL framework.

arxiv-2404-03934.title: Direct Electrical Detection of Spin Chemical Potential Due to Spin Hall Effect in β \beta -Tungsten and Platinum Using a Pair of Ferromagnetic and Normal Metal Voltage Probes
arxiv-2404-03934.creator: Soumik Aon, Abu Bakkar Miah, Arpita Mandal, Harekrishna Bhunia, Dhananjaya Mahapatra, Partha Mitra
arxiv-2404-03934.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Soumik Aon, Abu Bakkar Miah, Arpita Mandal, Harekrishna Bhunia, Dhananjaya Mahapatra, Partha Mitra. The phenomenon of Spin Hall Effect (SHE) generates a pure spin current transverse to an applied current in materials with strong spin-orbit coupling, although not detectable through conventional electrical measurement. An intuitive Hall effect like measurement configuration is implemented to directly measure pure spin chemical potential of the accumulated spins at the edges of heavy metal (HM) channels that generates large SHE.

arxiv-2407-02930.title: Timely Requesting for Time-Critical Content Users in Decentralized F-RANs
arxiv-2407-02930.creator: Xingran Chen, Member, IEEE, Kai Li, Kun Yang*, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2407-02930.description: Abstract With the rising demand for high-rate and timely communications, fog radio access networks (F-RANs) offer a promising solution. This work investigates age of information (AoI) performance in F-RANs, consisting of multiple content users (CUs), enhanced remote radio heads (eRRHs), and content providers (CPs).

arxiv-2409-04578.title: Parallax : A Compiler for Neutral Atom Quantum Computers under Hardware Constraints
arxiv-2409-04578.creator: Jason Ludmir, Tirthak Patel
arxiv-2409-04578.description: Abstract Among different quantum computing technologies, neutral atom quantum computers have several advantageous features, such as multi-qubit gates, application-specific topologies, movable qubits, homogenous qubits, and long-range interactions. However, existing compilation techniques for neutral atoms fall short of leveraging these advantages in a practical and scalable manner.

arxiv-2409-12515.title: Random Markov property for random walks in random environments
arxiv-2409-12515.creator: Julien Allasia, Rangel Baldasso, Oriane Blondel, Augusto Teixeira
arxiv-2409-12515.description: Abstract We consider random walks in dynamic random environments and propose a criterion which, if satisfied, allows to decompose the random walk trajectory into i.i.d. increments, and ultimately to prove limit theorems. The criterion involves the construction of a random field built from the environment, that has to satisfy a certain random Markov property along with some mixing estimates.

arxiv-2411-09318.title: DriveThru: a Document Extraction Platform and Benchmark Datasets for Indonesian Local Language Archives Thanks: Corresponding author
arxiv-2411-09318.creator: Mohammad Rifqi Farhansyah 1, Muhammad Zuhdi Fikri Johari 2, Afinzaki Amiral 3
arxiv-2411-09318.description: Abstract Indonesia is one of the most diverse countries linguistically. However, despite this linguistic diversity, Indonesian languages remain underrepresented in Natural Language Processing (NLP) research and technologies. In the past two years, several efforts have been conducted to construct NLP resources for Indonesian languages.

arxiv-2412-03694.title: Bidiagonal matrix factorisations related to multiple orthogonal polynomials
arxiv-2412-03694.creator: Amílcar Branquinho 1, Juan E.F. Díaz 2, Ana Foulquié-Moreno 3, Hélder Lima 4, Manuel Mañas 5
arxiv-2412-03694.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Amílcar Branquinho 1, Juan E.F. Díaz 2, Ana Foulquié-Moreno 3, Hélder Lima 4, Manuel Mañas 5. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the Hessenberg recurrence matrix associated with a system of multiple orthogonal polynomials to admit a factorisation as a product of bidiagonal matrices.

arxiv-2504-16348.title: Supermassive Binaries in Ultralight Dark Matter Solitons
arxiv-2504-16348.creator: Russell Boey 1, Emily Kendall 1, Yourong Wang 1,2, Richard Easther 1
arxiv-2504-16348.description: Abstract Ultralight (or fuzzy) dark matter (ULDM) is an alternative to cold dark matter. A key feature of ULDM is the presence of solitonic cores at the centers of collapsed halos. These would potentially increase the drag experienced by supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries, changing their merger dynamics and the resulting gravitational wave background.

arxiv-2506-04257.title: Deformation Due to Non-planar Fault Movement in Fractional Maxwell Medium
arxiv-2506-04257.creator: Pabita Mahato, Seema Sarkar (Mondal), Subhash Chandra Mondal
arxiv-2506-04257.description: Abstract In earthquake-prone regions, the accumulation of geophysical stress during the aseismic period plays a critical role in determining which faults are more likely to be reactivated in future seismic events. In this model, we consider an infinite non-planar fault located in a viscoelastic half-space of a fractional Maxwell medium representing the lithosphere-asthenosphere system comprising three interconnected planar sections.

arxiv-2511-02651.title: Apriel–H1: Towards Efficient Enterprise Reasoning Models Thanks: Correspondence to oleksiy.ostapenko@servicenow.com , contributors are listed in Section 6
arxiv-2511-02651.creator: SLAM Lab
arxiv-2511-02651.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve remarkable reasoning capabilities through transformer architectures with attention mechanisms. However, transformers suffer from quadratic time and memory complexity in the attention module (MHA) and require caching key-value states during inference, which severely limits throughput and scalability.

arxiv-2605-27030.title: Share More, Search Less: Collaborative Parallel Thinking for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
arxiv-2605-27030.creator: Xinglin Wang, Hao Lin, Shaoxiong Feng, Peiwen Yuan, Yiwei Li, Jiayi Shi, Yueqi Zhang, Chuyi Tan, Ji Zhang, Boyuan Pan, Yao Hu, Kan Li

arxiv-2606-22207.title: Lexical Consensus: Grounded Word Learning and Shared Meaning in Artificial Agents
arxiv-2606-22207.creator: P. M. Vera

govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIDallasFieldO.creator: Harold Weisberg
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIDallasFieldO.description: June 11, 1980 letter from Harold Weisberg to Julia Shea on the FBI Dallas field office's partial compliance with his Privacy Act requests and its withholding of records.

plos-pone-0349685.title: Evolving graph attention networks for dynamic link prediction
plos-pone-0349685.creator: Yucai Jiang, Rongying Shan, Gang Fu, Zhuolin Li, Jingjing Sun, Zhongyun Bao, Feifei Wei
plos-pone-0349685.description: Evolving graph attention networks for dynamic link prediction

pmc-10600850.title: Multi-organ hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia: A case report
pmc-10600850.creator: Ying-Ling Chen, Hong-Yue Jiang, Dong-Ping Li, Jiang Lin, Yun Chen, Li-Li Xu, Hong Gao
pmc-10600850.description: BACKGROUNDType 2 hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is a rare autosomal dominant disease and is associated with ALK1 gene mutations. Type 2 HHT patients primarily suffer from recurrent bleeding. There is currently no promising treatment.CASE SUMMARYA 5-year-old Chinese patient (III23) was admitted to Zhongshan Hospital for recurrent melena occurring over 2 mo.

pmc-11402136.title: Harnessing the power of AI and IoT for real-time CO2 emission monitoring
pmc-11402136.creator: Kaizhe Fan, Quanjun Li, Zhen Le, Qian Li, Jianfeng Li, Ming yan
pmc-11402136.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Global CO2 emissions have been an essential topic of the environmental discussion. Still, empirical data is needed to support arguments that high-quality government actions could reduce these emissions. By analyzing data from 137 nations from 2000 to 2020, we offer strong evidence that state policies focused on promoting healthy ecosystems, sustainable economic growth, and transcendent legislative changes are capable of decreasing CO2 emissions.

pmc-11446103.title: Impact of diverse aerobic exercise plans on glycemic control, lipid levels, and functional activity in stroke patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmc-11446103.creator: Kangcheng Chen, Yulong Wang, Dongxia Li, Jun Li, Yong Huang, Meiling Huang, Haifeng Ma
pmc-11446103.description: AimsThis study aimed to assess the effects of Low-to-Moderate Intensity Continuous Training (LMICT), Moderate-Intensity Interval Training (MIIT), and Reduced-Exertion High-Intensity Training (REHIT) on blood glucose regulation, functional recovery, and lipid levels in individuals who have experienced a stroke and are diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM).

pmc-11610847.title: Public’s perception and attitude toward genetic testing in Jazan region
pmc-11610847.creator: Ebtihal E. Eltyeb, Sami A. Alhazmi, Shahad H. I. Maafa, Sarah J. Mobarki, Nasser H. Sobaikhi, Rimas A. Sumayli, Khlood K. Alattas, Halah M. Shayani, Abdullah M. Alqahtani, Faris A. Alhazmi, Hafiz I. Al-Musawa
pmc-11610847.description: Background:With the advancements in genetic testing, a differentiated evaluation for susceptibility to diseases is becoming applicable to many disorders. Understanding the circumstances and promoting the widespread use of these tests in the Saudi setting requires understanding public opinion and attitudes. This study aimed to determine the perception and attitudes of the public in the Jazan region to genetic testing.

pmc-11657738.title: Digoxigenin activates autophagy in hepatocellular carcinoma cells by regulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway
pmc-11657738.creator: Mengqing Ma, Rui Hu, Qi Huang, Jing Li, Minling Lv, Jialing Sun, Xin Zhong, Jinyu Yi, Lanfen Peng, Wenxing Feng, Wenfeng Ma, Zhiyi Han, Wei Zhang, Xinfeng Sun, Bolin Zhan, Xingning Liu, Xiaozhou Zhou
pmc-11657738.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is recognized as a highly malignant tumor. Targeted combination immunotherapy, the initially approved regimen, is compromised by adverse side effects and low response rates during clinical treatment. Traditional Chinese medicine and its derived natural compounds, known for their anticancer effects, offer advantages of low toxicity and cost.

pmc-11848358.title: A RARE PRESENTATION OF TWO COLORECTAL ANOMALIES: ANORECTALMALFORMATION CO-EXISTING WITH HIRSCHSPRUNG'S DISEASE IN IBADAN
pmc-11848358.creator: K.I. Egbuchulem, T.A. Lawal, O.O. Ogundoyin, D.I. Olulana, A.O. Takure, O.T. Ojediran, H.D. Ogundipe
pmc-11848358.description: Background:The association of Hirschsprung's disease with anorectal malformation (ARM) is both diagnostically and surgically challenging, in addition to it being a rarity. Symptoms attributable to post-repair of ARM may mask the underlying Hirschsprung's disease (HD) and become worse after closure of stoma.

pmc-12402258.title: Correspondence of high dimensional emotion structures elicited from video clips between humans and multimodal LLMs
pmc-12402258.creator: Haruka Asanuma, Naoko Koide-Majima, Ken Nakamura, Takato Horii, Shinji Nishimoto, Masafumi Oizumi
pmc-12402258.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Recent studies have revealed that human emotions exhibit a high-dimensional, complex structure. A full capturing of this complexity requires new approaches, as conventional models that disregard high dimensionality risk overlooking key nuances of human emotions. Here, we examined the extent to which the latest generation of rapidly evolving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) capture these high-dimensional, intricate emotion structures, including capabilities and limitations. Specifically, we compared self-reported emotion ratings from participants watching videos with model-generated estimates (e.g., Gemini or GPT).

pmc-12741108.title: Deep learning, deeper relief: pipeline toward tailored analgesia for experimental animal models
pmc-12741108.creator: Luisa Barleben, Mareike Simon, Lisa Drees, Franziska Flohr, Christoph Jochum, Michela Di Virgilio, Frank Tacke, Sonja Bröer, Jana Wolf, Marina Kolesnichenko
pmc-12741108.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Effective pain management in animal models is crucial for maintaining ethical and scientific integrity. However, commonly used analgesics may affect immune responses and disturb signaling pathways, thereby potentially confounding the experimental outcomes. In mouse colitis models, opioids and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs have been shown to interfere with the immune response and the activation of the central regulator of inflammation, the transcription factor nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB).

pmc-12882290.title: Exploring social network factors impacting the implementation of communication supports designed for minimally verbal autistic preschool children: a study protocol
pmc-12882290.creator: Sarah Dufek, Aubyn C Stahmer, Giacomo Vivanti, Elizabeth McGhee Hassrick
pmc-12882290.description: BackgroundAutism is a lifelong condition and can lead to particularly severe disability for minimally verbal (MV) children. Prior research suggests that early intervention is critical for autistic children; yet long-term outcomes have been variable. This variability may be due to poor implementation of evidence-based strategies within the child’s community, however research examining this idea is limited.

pmc-13190822.title: Effect of mineralization of Erythrina poeppigiana particles and accelerated carbonation on the properties of fiber cement
pmc-13190822.creator: Lúcia Maria Joaquim Assane, Ianca Oliveira Borges, Felipe Gomes Batista, Lorran de Sousa Arantes, Murilo Daniel de Mello Innocentini, Ricardo Gabriel de Almeida Mesquita, José Benedito Guimarães Junior, Lourival Marin Mendes
pmc-13190822.description: Fiber cement is widely used in the construction industry due to its satisfactory physical and mechanical properties. However, the need to enhance these characteristics has driven research focused on the development of new additives and the optimization of manufacturing processes. In this context, the present study aimed to develop and evaluate extruded fiber cement composites reinforced with Erythrina poeppigiana particles.

pmc-13328452.title: Gate-tunable giant negative magnetoresistance in tellurene driven by quantum geometry
pmc-13328452.creator: Marcello B. Silva Neto, Chang Niu, Marcus V. O. Moutinho, Pierpaolo Fontana, Claudio Iacovelli, Victor Velasco, Caio Lewenkopf, Peide D. Ye
pmc-13328452.description: Negative magnetoresistance in conventional two-dimensional electron gases is a well known phenomenon, but its origin in complex and topological materials endowed with nontrivial quantum geometry remains elusive. Here, we report a giant negative magnetoresistance reaching −90% of the zero-field resistance, R0, in n-type tellurene films.

pmc-13376499.title: Successful Management of Refractory Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome With Topical Capsaicin: A Case Report With Proposed Mechanism of Action and Literature Review
pmc-13376499.creator: Muhammad ilyas, Anushka Fernando, Abubakir Choriyev, Mohammad Adi, Ahmed Ashraf
pmc-13376499.description: IntroductionCannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) is a debilitating disorder of chronic, heavy cannabis users characterized by cyclic severe nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain that is classically relieved by hot baths. Standard antiemetics often fail, and dysregulation of endocannabinoid signaling with involvement of heat-sensitive TRPV1 channels has been proposed.

pmc-13514545.title: Numerical Investigation of Gas–Liquid Multiphase Flow Characteristics and Nozzle Structure Optimization for a Multi-Hole Oxygen Lance in a Vanadium Extraction Converter
pmc-13514545.creator: Bowen Peng, Libin Yang, Jie Wang, Xiangchen Li, Chengyi Wang, Dengyu Niu, Congcong Zhang
pmc-13514545.description: HighlightsThe transient multiphase fluid dynamics and bath stirring mechanisms in a 200-t vanadium extraction converter were systematically quantified using a 3D CFD approach. * The aerodynamic interference and jet coalescence behaviors were critically compared between the central-hole (“3+1”) and conventional 3-hole nozzle configurations.

pmc-13591146.title: Myosteatosis in type 1 diabetes: immunometabolic mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets
pmc-13591146.creator: Fatema Al-Rashed, Halemah AlSaeed, Kevin Patrick Fennelly, Fahd Al Mulla, Rasheed Ahmad
pmc-13591146.description: Myosteatosis, defined as pathological lipid accumulation within and between skeletal muscle fibers, is increasingly recognized as a determinant of impaired muscle quality, metabolic inflexibility, and adverse clinical outcomes. Although well described in ageing, obesity, and cancer, its relevance to type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains underexplored.
